successors.note: 'Corinth and Chalcis, which were among the other combatants, both received Macedonian garrisons' (Chaeronea page, 338); the city stayed a polis, the seat of the League of Corinth ('all members became allied to each other, and to Macedon'). The Hellenistic Corinth (Ptolemy 308, Demetrius 304, Gonatas 245/44, Achaean League 243, Rome 146) is in antigonid-dynasty and achaean-league.

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria has no Corinth (it lies in Greek City-States and, in part, in the Peloponnesian League row). The page gives no area ('Area in km2: not given'); the 22 km disc round Corinth (1,520 km2) is the researcher's reading of Corinthia. Colonies (Corcyra and Syracuse in 733, Ambracia, Potidaea under Periander) were separate cities and are not drawn.

region.text: Corinthia: the Isthmus and the Corinthian territory (22 km disc round Corinth, 1,520 km2)

ledger.note: 747: Corinth becomes a unified state under the Bacchiads. 'During Bacchiad rule from 747 to 650 BC, Corinth became a unified state'; the Bacchiads were 'the ruling kinship group of archaic Corinth in the 8th and 7th centuries BC'. In 733 'Corinth established colonies at' Corcyra and Syracuse. The land (Corinthia) is a reading.

657: Cypselus seizes power and the Bacchiad oligarchy gives way to the Cypselid tyranny. 'In 657 BC, polemarch Cypselus obtained an oracle from Delphi' (the page also gives 658-628 and 'r. 657-627'). No territory changes hands in the page.
581: the tyranny ends. Periander's nephew 'was assassinated, ending the tyranny' (Timeline); the page does not give 584.

region.text: Corinthia: the Isthmus and the Corinthian territory (22 km disc round Corinth, 1,520 km2)

ledger.note: 338: Philip II garrisons Corinth after Chaeronea. 'Corinth and Chalcis, which were among the other combatants, both received Macedonian garrisons'; the League of Corinth was formed in 337 ('all members became allied to each other, and to Macedon'). The year is the battle's; the garrison is undated on the page beyond 'Philip also made peace with the other combatants'.

wars.name: Corinthian War
wars.outcome: 'In 395 BC, after the end of the Peloponnesian War, Corinth and Thebes' moved to support Athens in the Corinthian War; the page gives no end year or territorial change.
wars.note: peloponnesian-league records Corinth leaving in 395 and returning under the 387 King's Peace; Corinth 'switching back to the Peloponnesian League, joined Sparta' in 379 (this page).

certainty.note: No page gives any frontier of Corinthia.

sources.note: Macedonian garrisons at Corinth and Chalcis; League of Corinth.

notes: Archaic and classical Corinth only: the independent polis to the Macedonian garrison of 338, the end of this group's scope plus the garrison. The sources opened give the Hellenistic Corinth (captured from the Antigonids by Ptolemy I in 308, recaptured by Demetrius in 304, retaken by Gonatas in winter 245/44, brought into the Achaean League by Aratus in 243, 'permanently' after Roman intervention in 197, demolished in 146) but those are the Antigonid and Achaean dossiers' events (antigonid-dynasty, achaean-league already carry them). The territory is a reading (the page gives no km2). Colonies are not drawn because no page dates their independence; Syracuse (733) is syracuse (Cliopatria). Peloponnesian-league has Corinth as an ally 550-395, 387-366. Gazetteer: used place Corinth (resolves).
